In majordomus_cli::mesh::build_cache

majordomus_cli::mesh::build_cache

Module env 

Source
Expand description

The sccache client configuration, derived from the selected store (I2673, ADR 0157).

Derived, never typed. report answers what a compiler cache client on this machine should be configured with now: the local disk as the first level and, only when every condition below holds, the store select chose as the second. Nothing is written anywhere; the answer is variables for the environment of the process that starts the sccache server, and ~/.cargo/config.toml is never touched (ADR 0157, alternatives).

The second level is a start-up decision. sccache fixes its chain when its server starts and refuses to start when an S3 level does not answer then (measured on 0.17.0 and 0.18.0: the compile exits 2). A store that stops while the server runs is harmless (a miss). So the second level is handed over only when all of these hold at this moment, and the answer says which one did not when it is not:

  1. sccache answers --version;
  2. the node file (outside the repository) offers or knows a store, and select chooses one: the store answered its readiness route within the budget, so an unknown is never taken for healthy;
  3. a credential file exists, is a regular file readable by its owner alone, and holds the profile PROFILE;
  4. the installed sccache has the multi-level chain, which is measured, not assumed: a throwaway server is started on a private port with a chain naming a level that does not exist, and an sccache that knows the chain refuses it by name where one that does not simply starts.

No secret. The credential is named by the path of its file (AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE) and a profile; the file is opened only to see that the profile is in it, and nothing read from it is kept. An exported key is readable in every compiler’s environment, in ps eww and in every build script, so no key is ever exported.

§Example

use majordomus_cli::mesh::build_cache::env::{report, EnvOptions, Mode};
// no sccache here: the build is exactly what it was, and the answer says why
let answer = report(&EnvOptions {
    sccache: "/no/such/sccache".into(),
    node_file: None,
    credentials: None,
});
assert_eq!(answer.mode, Mode::LocalOnly);
assert!(answer.variables.is_empty());

Structs§

EnvOptions
What report reads: the sccache executable to ask, and optionally the node file and the credential file to use instead of the defaults under the user’s home.
EnvReport
The answer of report.
EnvVar
One variable of the client’s environment.
Sccache
What the installed sccache is, as measured.

Functions§

default_credentials
Where this node keeps its own client credential, an AWS-format file.
default_node_file
Where this node keeps what it offers and knows.
report
What the sccache client of this machine should be configured with now. Cheapest check first, so the usual local-only answer costs no process but sccache --version.
script
The report as a POSIX script that eval can read: one comment line and one export per variable, every value single-quoted. It runs nothing and assigns only the variables.
